text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Node k8s-gpu-17 in us-east-1 is reporting 95% ephemeral storage usage and started evicting pods (oom/killing). Triggered by /nodes/eviction-monitor.
maya: seeing lots of runtime pods OOM/crashloop on that node, model-cache writes spiking. Customers hitting errors 503/timeout.
sam: paging oncall. @oncall you up?
oncall: I'm on. Pulling logs now.
kevin: adding myself. Looks like model cache writes + logs filled /var/lib/docker overlay. Container restarts cause CUDA errors after hot restart — runtime can't warm kv-cache.
rachel: customer SLAs: a handful of Dedicated customers in us-east reporting increased latency and failed requests. Not P0 for platform-wide but impacting critical routes.
maya: can we cordon the node and evict remaining runtime pods to spread load? Want to avoid mass evictions at once.
ops_lead: agree cordon, then drain with grace and move heavy model pods first.
sam: running drain: 
```
kubectl cordon k8s-gpu-17
kubectl drain k8s-gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```
infra-bot: Notice: Node k8s-gpu-17 cordoned by sam at 2026-03-15T14:13:05Z.
maya: after drain, we should clear cache tmp files on the node and restart docker runtime.
kevin: grabbing node console. Disk usage shows /var/lib/docker/overlay2 at 98%. Large files are model shards and rotated logs in /var/log/redwood/runtime.
ops_lead: is there a quick cleanup that won't lose cache that still in use? We can delete stale model temp dirs older than 30m.
kevin: running find to list big dirs: 
```
ssh node-17
sudo du -h /var/lib/docker | sort -h | tail -20
sudo ls -lt /var/log/redwood/runtime | head -40
```
rachel: notifying affected customers (ticket flow) — tagging CSM.
oncall: noticed a few pods are crashlooping with GPU OOM and error: "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" right after container restart. Likely KV cache warmup tries to mmap too much.
maya: mitigation plan: 1) cordon/drain node 2) delete stale tmp/cache > 30m on node 3) restart docker + kubelet 4) scale up capacity (launch a new warm node) 5) rollout temporary model-variant with lower mem/quantized variant for affected routes.
sam: I'm provisioning 2 spot-warm nodes in us-east group now. ETA ~6m.
infra-bot: Auto-scaling: 2 nodes requested for pool gpu-us-east-warm; expected ready in ~5 minutes.
kevin: while nodes spin up, I'll safely remove large rotated logs: 
```
sudo find /var/log/redwood/runtime -type f -mmin +30 -delete
sudo rm -rf /var/lib/docker/tmp/*
```
maya: be careful with rm -rf — confirm the path.
kevin: confirmed, deleting only rotated logs and runtime tmp folders. Monitoring docker disk after each op.
ops_lead: also lower model cache write concurrency for runtime service to reduce pressure: set env REDWOOD_CACHE_WRITES=2 temporarily.
rachel: are we going to route traffic away from Dedicated customers on that node?
oncall: switching routing policy to avoid us-east-gpu-17 node group for canary customers. Doing canary shift for 5 minutes.
sam: new nodes are coming up. Spawning extra runtime pods and balancer will reassign.
incident-bot: NOTE: New node k8s-gpu-19 registered in pool gpu-us-east-warm at 2026-03-15T14:18:22Z.
kevin: after cleanup docker free space at 52%. Restarting kubelet and runtime.
kevin: restarting runtime pods on that node to reattach persistent caches where applicable.
oncall: I see crashloops drop. Error rates for affected routes falling back to baseline.
maya: rolling a hotfix to runtime to cap mmap size to avoid full memory map on restart. Pushing config change to canary 10%.
ops_lead: also enable logrotate immediate for runtime logs: rotate size 50M and keep 5.
sam: craft short customer comms: "We've mitigated a storage-pressure issue in us-east. Some requests were failing for a subset of customers between 14:12-14:22 UTC; routing and node remediation completed, and we're monitoring. Follow-up will include durable model cache and improved log rotation."
rachel: posting to status page now.
incident-bot: Incident severity set to Sev2 by ops_lead. Paging policy: all oncall notified.
oncall: handing off to @maya for post-incident monitoring and postmortem. I'm AFK.
maya: taking over. I'll keep watch for 30m and then start a postmortem draft.
kevin: plan for long-term fix: migrate model cache to ephemeral but persistent volume (local PV) with eviction thresholds, and add periodic scrubbing job for logs and tmp. Also add threshold alerts at 70% ephemeral usage.
ops_lead: add regression alert tied to runtime crashloop and CUDA OOM so we get paged earlier.
rachel: filing customer impact summary and will attach request IDs.
maya: link to follow-up runbook and todo items: create PV migration ticket, add alert, tune cache write concurrency, and ensure CI tests simulate node disk pressure.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: Node storage pressure mitigated and routing restored at 2026-03-15T14:26:03Z.
maya: thanks everyone. Postmortem draft incoming.
kevin: leaving notes in ops channel with the exact cleanup commands we ran and file sizes.
 rachel: closing customer tickets and adding credits where appropriate.
maya: small follow-up: we should test cache warmup behavior after sudden restart to avoid repeated CUDA errors.
